COLLEGE OF EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL STUDIES: Early Childhood Education: Since the relocation of the Early Childhood Education (ECE) to the School of Education, there have been many changes in the Human Development and Family Science courses required for the Early Childhood Education.
In addition, some changes made are not accurately presented in eCampus.
Thus, this request is to update courses required for a BS in ECE and a TCP, Pre-K-2 certificate.
We removed four Human development and Family Science courses (HDF 201, 202, 205, and 230) and update the course numbers and titles in the ECE curriculum for both programs (BS & TCP).
Health and Physical Education: We propose to reduce the total credits required for Health and Physical Education (HPE) students from 124 to 120.

This request is the result of the recently approved (12/9/2021) Anatomy/physiology requirement for HPE students.
Specifically, we are now requiring all HPE students to take KIN122 (3 credits) (Human Anatomy and Physiology) instead of BIO 220/221 (4 credits) and BIO222/223 (4 credits).
That change allows us to reduce the total number of credits for HPE students to 120 which is the minimum number of credits required for graduation as stated in our university manual 8.21.10.
Undergraduate Curricular Requirement.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: BS Nutrition and BS Dietetics: Currently, NFS offers a 3cr General Nutrition (NFS 207), and a 4cr Applied General Nutrition (NFS 210) course.
BS Nutrition and BS Dietetics students are required to take the four-credit course.
A Course Change Form has been submitted to change NFS 210 to a 1cr lab to be taken concurrently with the NFS 207 lecture.
We are making this change to increase instructional efficiency in the department.
The major requirements must be changed to reflect the change to NFS 207 (3) + NFS 210 (1).

COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: BS in Chemical Engineering: (1) Removing the Biology and Pharmaceutical Tracks for a B.S. in Chemical Engineering and moving to a single B.S. curriculum track for all programs.
These tracks are no longer necessary as CHE undergraduate students can receive minors in comparable subjects through established programs and new minors recently approved at URI.
Minors are better understood by potential employers and graduate programs and will be on students’ transcripts and diplomas, which is similar to how the Biology and Pharmaceutical Tracks were presented.

The coursework and knowledge gained using minors instead of degree tracks will be the same, but will also be more flexible for students. (2) To accommodate students pursuing the Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Minor and other new minors, we are adding the following course options for professional electives: 300-level or higher in BPS and a clarification of which natural sciences course can be used, including: AFS, AVS, BES, BIO, CHM, CMB, EVS, GEO, NEU, NRS, PLS, PHY, and SAF. (3) Science elective options are being expanded to include BIO 352, 437; BPS 312, 446; CMB 320 (Computational Bio), 341, 437 (Molecular Bio), 482 (Proteins and Enzymes); and PHY 540 (Modern Bio Phys).
PHY 530 is being removed from the list.
This will allow for more flexibility for students in their elective options and in pursuing the various minors CHE students might be interested in pursuing.
BS in Mechanical Engineering: Several small changes to the curriculum: 1.
Replace MTH 244 (differential equations) with MTH 362 (advanced engineering mathematics) in the sophomore spring. 2.
Update the list of courses acceptable as a professional elective (footnote 3). (See Appendix E) (See Appendix F) (See Appendix G) (See Appendix H) (See Appendix I)

3 COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT MINOR: Students in the International Development minor are trained to successfully address global challenges associated with international development. Through a combination of coursework, practical experience and study abroad, students gain in-depth knowledge of and experiences associated with the social, cultural, political, and economic challenges in the global South. The International Development minor is an existing program within CELS that, over the last two decades, has been housed in the Natural Resources Science Department. However, with the departure of its key instructor and the minor coordinator, in 2019 the administration of the minor changed from the NRS department to the MAF department, and MAF has hired a coordinator (Assistant Professor, International Development) starting Spring 2021 to further develop the program. The coordinator complements existing teaching and research capacity within Dept of Marine Affairs. The existing structure of the minor is as follows (includes a total of 18 credits with a maximum of six credits at the 100- or 200- level): 3 credits of MAF350/NRS 300 6 credits of language requirement 3-6 credits of electives Approved Internship, research project, or study abroad experience (MAF/NRS 450) We are requesting that the required seminar MAF 496 be reinstated to become a required course for the minor. We are also requesting that the language requirement be waived for students who have grown up multilingual or who have lived in a foreign country. The other requirements will stay the same.
